The system subs and other popular subs are healthy, but I'm interested in driving traffic to smaller subs as well. To that end whenever I find a link to post in a large sub, I try to think of a smaller sub it could also go in and post it there first, cross-posting to the larger sub. That way, the smaller sub gets content it wouldn't have gotten otherwise, plus a bit of exposure, and doesn't require a lot of extra effort on my part.

My question is, what's the most respectful/unobtrusive way to cross-post content so that it doesn't detract from the larger sub?
What's the most respectful/unobtrusive way to cross-post content and promote smaller subs?

I used to include "x-post from /v/SmallSub" in the title of the post, but I wonder if that's too obtrusive. Lately I've just been including "x-post from /v/SmallSub" as a comment in the post instead. It doesn't give the small sub the visibility that the reference in the title does, but it has the benefit of being clickable and it doesn't clutter up the front page of the large sub with "x-post" references. I figure anyone who is interested enough in the content to click on the comments might be interested in checking out the related smaller sub as well.

Edit: I've also seen people link directly to the post created in the smaller sub, but I don't really like that idea because it makes people "double jump" to get to the content. It works out well if you're cross-posting a discussion question and want to keep the discussion on the small sub, but for news stories I'd rather just cross-post the link itself.
